questions: What does "possible value" mean - should we output the maximum achievable value, minimum achievable value, or all possible values?
Can we choose the same position i multiple times across different operations, or must each position be chosen at most once?
Is there a requirement to use exactly M operations, or can we stop early if we've achieved our desired result?
When multiple positions yield the same digit during an operation, which position should we choose?
Should the final output be formatted with leading zeros if the first digit becomes zero after operations?
What happens if M > N - do we process all M operations even when we've already modified all positions in S?
Is there a specific tie-breaking rule when multiple strategies lead to the same optimal value?
Should we consider all possible choices of positions across all operations, or is there a greedy strategy implied?

You will perform the following operation for k=1,2,\ldots,M in order: Choose an integer i such that 1 \le i \le N. Then, replace the i-th character of S with the k-th character of T. Note that the choice of i for each k is not addressed by the given clarification; typically this would mean the maximum achievable value, but that's not explicitly confirmed here. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N M S T Output Print the possible value of the resulting string S interpreted as an integer after performing the M operations. Constraints - 1 \le N,M \le 10^6 - N and M are integers. - S is a string of length N consisting of digits from 1 through 9. - T is a string of length M consisting of digits from 1 through 9.
